sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:7

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:7:1
items.html: the first three of the six extremities of AA of Beria, which are HGT: All the ten Sefirot of Beria are at the stature of the light of Bina, even Keter and Hochma (as above, Chapter 4, item 2). And since the stature of Bina of Atzilut clothes upon HGT of AA, nothing can be extended from it to the world of Beria except HGT NHY alone, which are its VAK. Therefore HGT of AA of Beria are considered as the GAR of AA that is there, and it will be further explained in its place.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:7:2
items.html: revealed without clothing: The Rosh of every Partzuf does not clothe in the Partzuf below it, for the clothing of the lower one begins from the mouth of the Rosh of the upper one and downward, as written in its place. And since HGT of AA are a Rosh, they are therefore revealed without clothing.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:7:3
items.html:
did not pierce that screen: Piercing means the overpowering of the light over the boundary in the screen, so that it pays no heed to the power of restraint in it, and it bursts through and passes and shines even below the screen. And you must recall well what we explained above, in the explanation of the striking of the upper light against the screen (in Ohr Penimi, Chapter 2, item 3), that the screen stops the upper light, which spreads to pass even below its boundary, and returns it to its place, as above in the words of the Rav (Section III, Chapter 1, item 3). Now, with all this, some part of the upper light burst forth and did not return, but descended below the screen and shone there — which resembles as though it had pierced and broken and made a hole in the body of the screen, and passed its way from there downward. However, there is no resemblance here at all to a piercing and a hole in a physical, imagined, and sensed sense, God forbid, but it is a matter of overstepping a boundary alone: for the screen limits the light, as is known. And that small part of the upper light, which the screen did not limit and did not restrain, is termed as though this part pierced the screen — meaning, pierced its boundary and the restraint in it — and passed even below the screen.
And this part, which overstepped the boundary of the screen and passed downward, is termed by the name Malchut of Malchut of the upper degree, or the point of Malchut of the upper one.
Therefore we must distinguish, in the aforementioned coupling by striking, two aspects: the first aspect is that the screen overpowered the light and returned it to its place, whereby the reflected light became a garment over the four aspects in the upper light from below upward, by force of which Malchut expanded into ten Sefirot from itself and downward from the screen, in such a way that all the ten Sefirot that came out from the screen and upward had their illumination sparkle even below the screen, and stamped their image there from above downward, as above (in Ohr Penimi, Chapter 2, item 3) — and this is the first aspect in the coupling by striking.
The second aspect is that part of the upper light which broke and pierced the screen, and passed below the screen without the aid of reflected light, as above, but in the aspect of its very essence. That is, as explained above, that this part is called the point of Malchut of the upper one, or Malchut of Malchut of the upper one, which nullified the boundary and paid no heed at all to the power of restraint in the screen. And understand well that regarding that point, the screen is considered as though it did not exist at all, for the Rav therefore was precise in saying, "breaks and pierces the screen," for the reason explained. And by these two explained aspects, you will understand the entire continuation of the Rav's words.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:7:4
items.html: clothes in the first three of AA: That is, in HGT of AA, which are its GAR, because this AA of Beria has only VAK: HGT NHY alone, and its HGT are found to be its GAR, as above. And understand here, that that point of Malchut of Atzilut, which pierced and passed below the screen in the secret of the second aspect mentioned above, in the adjacent passage — this is the Ein Sof mentioned above by the name Tohu, which has of the aspect of Ein Sof, as above, and has none of the four aspects HB TM, but the four aspects are included in it "in potential" and not in actuality. And those GAR of AA mentioned above, in which the point of the upper one clothed, behold these GAR come from the first aspect mentioned above, in the adjacent passage, and are called "Bohu," and in it are the four roots of the four aspects HB TM "in actuality," that is, through the clothing of reflected light, which are the aspect of vessels in actuality — and remember this.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:7:5
items.html: the two luminaries: ZA and Malchut are called the two luminaries, for they influence the lower worlds, since the lower ones cannot receive from the GAR — Keter, Hochma, Bina — and therefore ZA and Malchut alone shine to the lower ones, and for this reason they are termed luminaries. And when they were emanated, their stature was equal to one another, meaning that Malchut received her flow from Bina, and not through ZA, in which manner the two were equal, for just as ZA was emanated from Bina and receives its flow from Bina, so too the Nukva receives her flow from Bina. But when Malchut is not fit to receive from Bina except through ZA, she is then considered to be below ZA, for the receiver is below its giver, as is understood, and the reason for this will be explained in its place.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:7:6
items.html:
the moon contended and was diminished: It was already explained in the adjacent passage, that the moon, which is the secret of Malchut, was equal with ZA, which is the secret of the sun, as above. Now at that time the stature of both of them was the stature of VAK: HGT NHY, both of them lacking a Rosh, lacking the first three, but they nursed from Bina, who is called Keter. And this is what our sages said (Chullin 60b), that she said, two kings cannot use one crown, namely Ima — but Malchut wished to rule alone, and it was then said to her, go and diminish yourself, meaning that she should go out from Atzilut to Beria, and there she would rule.
And whereas Malchut had been in Atzilut a complete Partzuf of ten Sefirot, she was diminished through her descent into Beria, and stood there in the secret of a small point comprised of ten Sefirot "in potential" and not in actuality. And this will be further explained ahead.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:7:7
items.html: the other nine points flew away from her: That is, they remained in ZA in Atzilut, and only the aspect of Malchut of Malchut descended to Beria.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:7:8
items.html: a mirror that has nothing of her own: Aspaklaria means "luminary," for Malchut is called a luminary as above. And it says that she has nothing of her own, because her root from the beginning is only a single point, as the Rav wrote before, and all the nine Sefirot that she had while still in Atzilut are not her own aspect, that is, not from the aspect of the direct light of Malchut, but only from the aspect of the reflected light that the screen raised from her upward to ZA — and this reflected light returns from ZA to Malchut from above downward, and builds Malchut into ten Sefirot (as above, in Ohr Penimi, Chapter 2, item 3). And this is what the Rav means in saying that through ZA nine other points were added to her. Therefore, when Malchut was diminished and descended to Beria, only the essence of Malchut descended, and all the first nine Sefirot, which are of the aspect of reflected light, remained in Atzilut in ZA at their root. This is what the Rav means: "and ZA took back" and took them. And this is why she is called a mirror that has nothing of her own.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:7:9
items.html: returned her face-to-face as at first: This is a lengthy matter that there is no room to explain here.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:7:10
items.html: anything of holiness leaves an imprint in its place: For the matter of absence does not apply to spiritual things, and any change or diminishment and the like — the meaning is not that the first aspect is annulled and in its place comes a new aspect, but the meaning is that the first aspect remains as it was, and the matter of change that we speak of in it is an additional aspect upon the first. In such a way, that wherever it is said that some aspect changed, the intent is that an aspect was added onto the first aspect. And this must be remembered, for it is impossible to mention it always. And this is what the Rav means: "everything of holiness leaves an imprint in its place, even though it has departed from there," and this aspect of the point always remained in the head of Beria — meaning, as explained, that the matter of the point's rising and returning to its place in Atzilut does not cause any absence in the point that descended to Beria, for there is no absence in spiritual things. And therefore one must understand the matter of the point's return to Atzilut as an additional matter that came into being anew, like one who lights a candle from a candle without the first being diminished — in such a way that the point remains in the head of Beria, and also rose to Atzilut, and now there are two points, and understand this well.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:7:11
items.html: a tail to lions at the end of Atzilut: That is, the end of all the Sefirot of Atzilut, which are pictured in a parable as compared to the Sefirot of Beria, like lions compared to foxes. And Malchut descended from the end of the Sefirot of Atzilut, and became a head to the Sefirot of Beria, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:7:12
items.html: Eve was a tail to Adam: ZA and Malchut are termed by the name Adam and Eve, and Malchut is the end of all the Sefirot of ZA, as above. Therefore our sages expounded, regarding Adam HaRishon before the creation of Eve, that Eve was a tail to Adam, meaning, the aspect of his end.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:7:13
items.html: that very Hochma descended and broke the screen: That is, the Malchut of AK, in which the screen of the third degree of coarseness is rectified, which is the stature of Hochma — that Malchut descended and became Atik in Atzilut.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:7:14
items.html: the Holy of Holies of Beria: The Rosh of Beria, in which the point of Malchut of Atzilut is clothed, is called the chamber of the Holy of Holies, and this entire chamber rises together with the point to Atzilut on the day of the Sabbath, by force of the point of Atzilut clothed there.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:7:15
items.html: in the language of negation, to exclude Keter: They should have said that reishit is Hochma, so why did they say "reishit is nothing but Hochma" — the meaning being, and nothing else: namely, "to exclude Keter," to teach you that Keter is not the reishit of the world, but Hochma is the reishit of the world, for the world too, taken as a whole, has the four aspects HB TM, of which Hochma is the first aspect among them, but Keter is not counted as an aspect of the world, but rather an intermediary as above, and it, by itself, likewise comprises the four aspects, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:7:16
items.html: the ten Sefirot divide into four letters of the Name: Indeed, the ten Sefirot do not divide into ten Partzufim, and the reason is that the six Sefirot HGT NHY do not make six Partzufim, since they are all only one aspect in the coarseness of the screen and in the measure of the stature, namely the third degree of coarseness. Therefore all of them together come out from one coupling by striking, and are therefore considered one Partzuf. And the matter of the distinction among the six Sefirot HGT NHY will be explained in the coming lessons, God willing.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:7:17
items.html: the four letters of the Name Havaya: The four letters of the Name Havaya are HB TM as above, and Tifferet alone comprises six Sefirot, and the intermediate aspect between Emanator and emanated is called Keter, and together they are ten Sefirot. And every particular Sefira of these ten Sefirot must necessarily itself be comprised of ten Sefirot, and so on in particulars of particulars, as was explained at length in Inner Observation, Part 2, item 96.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:7:18
items.html:
'Ein' [Nothing] and 'Ani' [I]: There is a most notable allusion here, for the word "Ein" [nothing] indicates the absence of grasping, and its opposite is the word "Ani" [I], which indicates the ultimate degree of grasping in its final perfection. And although you have no two matters more opposite and contradictory of one another than these two words "Ein Ani" [I am nothing], as explained, nevertheless their letters are equal and identical to one another, which is a most wondrous marvel. And this is the secret of the verse, "I am the first and I am the last," to teach that they are not at all two things, God forbid, but truly one, as the Rav writes: "for in the aspect of Malchut of the Emanator that is in it, it is last and is called 'Ani' [I], which is Malchut. And in the aspect of the root of the emanated beings that is in it, which is the aspect of Keter, it is first and is called 'Ein' [Nothing], which are the letters of 'Ani' [I]," end quote. And these words are deep beyond all depth and high beyond all height, and therefore the Rav alerts us here and says, "and understand this well, for through it all the discourses that we shall explain will be understood."
For one must understand very well the secret of these two opposite matters here, that they are not even two distinct aspects, but must be understood as one aspect: that from the side of its being the Malchut of the upper one and the very essence of the upper one, which broke and pierced the screen, as written above, so that upon the point of the Malchut of the upper one the power of the boundary in the screen has no effect whatsoever — for this reason it is called Keter, "Ani" [I], last, meaning the ultimate of perfection, for the Malchut of the upper one receives from all the ten Sefirot of the upper one, which ten Sefirot necessarily comprise all the degrees and Partzufim fit to spread into the worlds below them, and it is therefore found that that point is comprised of the final perfection, and this is "I am the last." And this is the secret of Keter, which is called Atik, and is called Tohu, and is called the spark of the Creator, and is called Ein Sof, blessed be He. But from the side of its being a root to the emanated beings that are in it, for it is the aspect of Keter to the emanated below it, this is the secret of "I am the first," which is called "Ein" [nothing], the letters of "Ani" [I] — meaning, that toward the emanated beings, those very letters of "Ani" [I] combine into the combination "Ein" [nothing], which is the opposite meaning of the combination "Ani" [I], since it too is the Malchut of the upper one, but from the aspect of "light diminishing and passing through the screen," as explained above at length — which for this reason comprises the four aspects HB TM in actuality, as above. Therefore it is called the Rosh of the emanated, for everything that exists in the body is drawn from the Rosh. And it is called "Ein" [nothing], for all the degrees and worlds below it go on revealing what is in the Rosh, and before they finish what is incumbent upon them, the Rosh is in the aspect of "Ein" [nothing], in the secret of 'I am the first,' meaning only the beginning of the revelation and the root for the revelation. And it is called Arich Anpin, and is called Bohu, and is called the spark of the created, and is called Keter — and be precise in these words, perhaps you will merit and find the gateway to wisdom. However, what is said, that the aspect of Atik is called 'I am the last,' this is said only from the aspect of its rising to Atzilut on the day of the Sabbath, when it returns and becomes there the Malchut of the upper one, as the Rav writes, and understand.
